game.title: Last Seat on Fortune Row
game.subtitle: Five houses. One way to make your name.
game.setting: A fictional private-poker circuit in 1947. Fortune Row is the players' nickname for five invitation-linked houses in Las Vegas, Hollywood, Mexico City, New York and postwar Paris.

introParagraphs: Las Vegas glows at the edge of the desert. You have $1,000, a change of clothes, and the kind of plan that sounds better after midnight.

They call it Fortune Row: five private games, linked by introductions rather than streets. The Gilded Alibi is your first open door. Hollywood, Mexico City, New York and Paris keep their guest lists close.
Win all four tables in a house, outlast its boss, and earn the next invitation. Passage and a room are included. You came to make a name that travels. Pick a chair, {name}.

rules.seatOrder: Randomized once at table creation; dealer button then follows the ordinary rules.
rules.reroll: Only on buying into a new table. Preserve IDs, seats, hands and memories in saves.
rules.passes: Permanent unlocks, not consumable keys. Replays cannot remove passes.
rules.failure: Losses keep table-clear stamps and passes. A house stake remains available under the economy plan.
rules.castBalance: Each current casino has five male and three female regulars. Four bosses are men; Celeste Varela remains the Mexico City boss.

avatars.title: The Drifter
avatars.description: You have carried your stake a long way. Fortune Row looks like a place where a stranger might finally make a name.
avatars.arrival: The bus left before dawn. You kept your suitcase, your stake, and a reason to see what lay beyond the station.

avatars.title: The Heiress
avatars.description: The invitation has always been easy. Earning your own reputation is the part that interests you.
avatars.arrival: For once, you have arrived without an introduction. You want the room to remember your name for something you earned.
avatars.portraitDescription: A wealthy white traveler aged 62, regal bony face, striking large aquiline nose, pale narrow eyes, pronounced cheekbones and a restrained, sly, asymmetrical smile. Straight silver jaw-length bob tucked tightly behind the ears beneath a small dark 1940s cocktail hat with a raised veil that does not obscure the face. Dark fur-collared coat and one long strand of pearls. Worldly, imposing and amused, not a youthful pinup.

avatars.title: The Pilot
avatars.description: You have learned to read the conditions and choose your moment. Tonight the destination is yours.
avatars.arrival: With your last fare delivered and your savings in your pocket, you followed the lights into Fortune Row.

avatars.title: The Reporter
avatars.description: You came looking for a story. Somewhere along the way, you decided to become part of it.
avatars.arrival: You have spent years writing about other people's big breaks. Tonight you intend to stop taking notes.
avatars.portraitDescription: ONE adult white WOMAN working as a reporter in 1947, aged 28. Clearly a woman with a strong rectangular freckled face, a crooked narrow nose, heavy eyebrows, an expressive wide mouth and a sharp open grin. Short rough blonde crop and a cowlick under a small narrow-brim felt hat tipped back, with a simple hairclip visible at one temple. Plain collared blouse with the top button open, a loosely tied thin patterned neck scarf and a battered wool jacket. NO facial hair, beard or stubble. Alert, irreverent, visibly tired and independent, never a glamorous curled-bob beauty.

avatars.title: The Crooner
avatars.description: You have worked the smaller stages and saved the tips. You are ready to see what the next room holds.
avatars.arrival: You left the microphone cooling on the stand and walked out with a pocketful of wages and one ambitious idea.

avatars.title: The Mechanic
avatars.description: You saved your stake one repair at a time. A steady hand and a little patience have served you well.
avatars.arrival: The garage lights went out behind you. For once, the money in your pocket is yours to risk.
avatars.portraitDescription: A rugged white male mechanic aged 43. Big square jaw, flattened crooked nose, thick dark stubble, short bristly dark hair, heavy brows and a grease smudge on his left cheek. Battered canvas work cap and dark oil-marked coveralls over a plain undershirt, with the small end of a wrench visible in a breast pocket. One eyebrow raised in a dry, confident squint.

avatars.title: The Dancer
avatars.description: You know how to hold a room's attention. Tonight you want a seat beyond the footlights.
avatars.arrival: The last show paid just enough. Tonight you have come to sit under a different kind of spotlight.
avatars.portraitDescription: A Black stage dancer aged 32 with a strong athletic neck, very sharp cheekbones, broad nose, small dimpled chin and a bright wide smile showing slightly uneven teeth. Hair tightly slicked flat into a small low bun, a narrow patterned headband tied in a small knot by the right ear, no waved coiffure. Simple sleeveless stage blouse with a striped shawl around the shoulders. Spirited, physically confident and full of character.

avatars.title: The Tailor
avatars.description: You have dressed plenty of winners. Now you intend to find out how it feels to be one.
avatars.arrival: You closed the shop, put on your best work, and brought the stake you stitched together over a long year.
avatars.portraitDescription: An adult South Asian man in his forties, neatly parted 1940s hair, trim mustache, a well-fitted waistcoat over a white collared shirt and tie, warm shrewd eyes.

avatars.title: The Night Nurse
avatars.description: Long shifts taught you patience and a calm face. The city has finally given you a night of your own.
avatars.arrival: Your shift is over. For the first time in weeks, the night belongs to you.
avatars.portraitDescription: A white night nurse aged 55. Broad heavy jaw, small round nose, deep under-eye shadows, strong gray eyebrows and a deeply lined, kind but no-nonsense face. Short frizzy gray hair pinned flat beneath a plain folded 1940s white nurse's cap, with no insignia or red-cross symbol. Simple period nursing collar and dark cardigan. A tired, crooked, encouraging smile, no glamour or salon waves.

avatars.title: The Gambler
avatars.description: You have played for small stakes in unfamiliar rooms. Fortune Row is the next step.
avatars.arrival: You have earned your stake in smaller rooms. This time, you mean to stay until the last chair is empty.
avatars.portraitDescription: An adult East Asian man in his thirties, neatly side-parted 1940s dark hair, dark waistcoat and open-collar white shirt, composed approachable face with a slight knowing smile.

casinos.name: The Gilded Alibi
casinos.description: A discreet desert card room: dark walnut, shaded lamps, desert light at the shutters, and your first open door.

boss.name: Victor "The House" Maddox
boss.portraitDescription: A broad, stocky Nevada man aged 58. Deep-set watchful eyes, heavy square jaw, pitted sun-weathered cheeks, a once-broken nose, deeply receding slick dark hair with gray temples and a clean-shaven chin. A short unlit cigar held at one corner of his closed mouth. Cream 1940s linen jacket, dark waistcoat, narrow Western string tie with a small horseshoe clasp. A dry, intimidating half-smile; the face of a former desert sports bookmaker who now owns the room.
boss.voice: Dry desert understatement. Quietly quotes the actual price and lets silence do the pressing.
boss.tell: Smooths his waistcoat when the room gets loud; never treats it as proof of his cards.
boss.greeting: Four tables first. Show me you can keep your seat, then we'll talk business.
boss.defeatLine: You earned this one fair and square. Take my card to the Marigold Star. Passage and a room are covered.
